page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor operating at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is modest, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the bottom 10% and single-threaded gzip compression in the bottom 25%. However, the 64 physical cores deliver robust parallel processing capabilities. The instance achieves strong results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, PassMark CPU encryption, and Geekbench ray tracing, all placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth remains stable, with both cached small-block and uncached large-block read/write operations scoring in the average range.

Given its high core density and 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the ecs.c6a.16xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads that do not require massive per-core memory footprints. The absence of local storage and GPUs represents a tradeoff, making it a specialized choice for compute-heavy tasks. It is suitable for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, ray tracing, and parallel data decompression, while being less optimal for single-threaded tasks or memory-intensive database operations.
